observations.observation: FAIR guidance addresses federation, standards and discoverable, reusable data.
Open Data Directive supplies reuse, licensing and high-value data context including transport.
INSPIRE supplies discovery criteria and metadata definitions, including services, spatial and temporal context, licences and conformance.
DCAT-AP supplies the extension baseline, multilingual representation and mandatory/optional catalogue concepts.
EU EIP CMC supplies 32 minimum metadata elements; its guideline and 2020 annual report discuss deployment variation and harmonisation obstacles.
The reviewed training introduces DCAT concepts, controlled vocabularies, obligations and extension conformance.
Reviewers considered the proposed DGA of limited direct relevance to the NAP scope at that time.
Reviewers considered the European data strategy of limited direct metadata relevance.
The FAIR-cost study discusses missing persistent identifiers, incomplete descriptions, interoperable standards and machine-readable metadata.
Riley and Baca provide general metadata and interoperability background.
SPRINT federation maps Belgian, Dutch and French NAP descriptions into a common catalogue.
SPRINT D2.3 examines NAP/CMC descriptions and formulates metadata competency questions.
The first LOD-RoadTran18 report reviews road-traffic models, ontologies and tooling.
The second LOD-RoadTran18 report compares ITS/PSI implementation and metadata approaches, including harvesting and conversion.
National and geospatial profiles illustrate extension structure and publication artifacts; their exact historical versions were not fully recorded.
TransportDCAT-AP supplies an earlier public-transport profile and constraints considered by reviewers.
Get ready for data presents questions about project strategy, collection/use, ethics and engagement.

note: 17 named numbered groups after §2.1 methodology. Report says 18 summaries/50 resources, but the private reference folder is not a complete one-to-one bibliography. These are review observations, not originals of reviewed sources.
